items.title: An extension which is a universal homeomorphism on spectra onto isomorphic residue fields contains an element outside the base whose square and cube lie in the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a ring extension whose spectrum map is a universal homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms on residue fields, and which is nontrivial, contains an element outside the base whose square and cube lie in the base (statement lines 11614-11620). The counted proof, 33 lines, is a chain of reductions with a genuine dichotomy: the extension is integral, one may assume it is generated by a single element and hence finite, one localizes at a minimal prime of the support of the quotient so that the support becomes the maximal ideal, and then the annihilator description of the support together with the homeomorphism hypothesis identifies the unique prime of the extension over the maximal ideal; an application of the consecutive-powers criterion finishes unless that prime is contained in the base, in which case the residue field hypothesis forces the two rings to be equal (proof lines 11623-11653). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof supplies checkable reductions and constructions rather than a restatement, and no clause of the statement is left to the reader.
